ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Facial swelling and difficulty breathing for two days with tea-colored urine

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents to the emergency department later on the same day as his outpatient pediatric evaluation for periorbital and lower extremity swelling. His parents note that his urine has been tea-colored since the symptoms began. He has no history of recent trauma or chronic illness but did have a sore throat about two weeks ago that resolved without medical attention.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of renal disease
- No family history of autoimmune disorders
- Noncontributory

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, his temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), blood pressure is 170/112 mm Hg, pulse is 128/min, and respirations are 38/min

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Auscultation reveals fine bilateral crackles at the lung bases. Cardiac exam reveals a normal S1 and S2 with no murmurs. There is periorbital edema and mild abdominal distension.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis shows numerous dysmorphic red blood cells and red cell casts. Serum creatinine is elevated at 1.6 mg/dL.

IMAGING:
A chest x-ray is shown.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Pediatric Nephrology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Recurrent swelling of face and legs progressively worsening over the past week

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to pediatric nephrology clinic six months following prior encounters for facial swelling and respiratory difficulty requiring emergency department evaluation. He is brought to the pediatrician by his mother due to swelling of his face and legs that has progressively worsened over the past week. The child had a sore throat 3 weeks ago, which resolved without antibiotics.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

His vaccinations are up to date.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of renal disease
- No family history of autoimmune disorders
- Noncontributory

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child appears well but has periorbital edema and 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis reveals hematuria, proteinuria, and red blood cell casts. Serum laboratory values are as follows:

- Serum creatinine: 1.8 mg/dL (normal: 0.3-0.7 mg/dL)
- Blood urea nitrogen (BUN): 40 mg/dL (normal: 5-18 mg/dL)
- Complement component 3 (C3): Decreased
- Antistreptolysin O (ASO) titer: Elevated
